newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA TO HOST WHEAT RESEARCH MEETING NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: INDIA TO HOST WHEAT RESEARCH MEETING NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Delegates from nearly 30 countries will participate in a three-day conference on wheat in India next week, focusing on new technologies to increase productivity and meet the country's growing needs.

The conference on 'Wheat Research Needs Beyond 2000 A.D.' will discuss an "action plan, strategies and technologies to ensure availability of wheat to the entire population at an affordable price and in adequate quantity", a statement from the organisers said.

About 200 scientists from India and abroad were expected to attend the conference organised by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) in the northern Indian town of Karnal from August 12 to 14.
"The conference will examine various options available for increasing the yield levels," it said.
Delegates from Australia, Austria, Belgium, Germany, Mexico, Switzerland, the United States, Thailand, Bangladesh and Nepal will participate.

ICAR said India's wheat requirement was expected to rise to about 109 million tonnes by 2020. "Hence, we have to add another 40 million tonnes to the present wheat production by 2020 to meet the need."

The statement said there was vast untapped potential in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, eastern state of Bihar and central state of Madhya Pradesh where wheat yields were currently two tonnes per hectare.
"This can be easily doubled," it said.
